div.l: His parishshenes deuouteli wold teche
Benigne he was and wondre diligent
And in aduersite ful pacient
And suche he was proued oft sithes
Ful loth were him to curs for his tithes
But raddar wold he gif oute of doute
To his propre ꝑparishens aboughte
Of his offering and of his substaunce
He couth in litul þing haue sustenaunce
Wide was his parissh and houses fer a sondr
But he left not for reyn̄ ne for thondr
In sikenesse or in myscheue to visite
The ferthest of his parish moche and lite
Vpon his fete and in his honde a staffe
This noble ensaumpe to his shepe he gafe
That first he wrought and afterward he taught
Oute of þe gospell thes wordes he caught
And þis figure he added eke þere to
That if gold rust what shuld Iren do
For if a prest be foule on whom we trust
No wondre is þough a leude man to rust
And shame it is if a prest take hede
A sheten sheperd and a clene herde shepe
Wele aught a prest ensaumpe for to gyue
Be his clawes how that his shepe shuld leue
He set not his benefis to hire
And lete his shepe be combred in þe mire
And ren to london to seint Paules
To seche him a chauntour for soules
Or with a brotherhede to halde
But dwelled at home and kept wel his folde
So þat þe wolf had it not to myscari
He was a shepard and not a mercenari
And though he holi were and vertuose
He was not to sinfull men dispitouse
Nor of his speche dangerus and digne
But in his speche discrete and benigne
To draw folke to heuen by fairenesse
Be goode ensaumpe this was his besinesse
But it were ony ꝑperson abstinate
Who so he were of hie and lowe estate
Him wold he snyb sharpeli for þe nones
A better prest I trow no where is
